<margin>Commentary by Su</margin> Not knowing yet striving to learn, hearing and seeing more each day without a way to unify it, one cannot avoid being burdened by it. Confucius said: "To hear much, select the good and follow it; to see much and remember it, this is the second tier of knowledge." If one day you know the Way, look back at those artificial pursuits; there is not one thing that is not false. To remove falsehood and restore one's nature is what is meant by "diminishing." Confucius said to Zigong: "Do you think I am one who learns much and remembers it?" Zigong replied: "Yes, is it not so?" Confucius said: "It is not. I unify it with one thread." To remove falsehood in order to restore one's nature can be called diminishing. Yet, if the intention to remove falsehood still exists, one has not yet reached the stage of forgetting both that and this. When the heart is pure and remains only as one's nature without remainder, then everything one does will not deviate from non-action (<term>wu wei</term> <gloss>effortless action/non-contrivance</gloss>). People all have the desire to control the principles and affairs of the world, so they create tasks and seek to control them; the heart manifests outwardly and the world dislikes it, so it can never be attained. The Sage practices non-action, so he has no tasks. His heart does not manifest outwardly and the world is at peace. Although he does not seek to control the principles and affairs of the world, he acts upon them, and the principles and affairs of the world become orderly and peaceful accordingly.

<margin>Commentary by Lü</margin> Those who engage in learning have not yet heard the Way. Because they have not heard the Way and seek it, they must increase their knowledge day by day. Those who engage in the Way have already heard the Way. Because they have already heard the Way and practice it, they aim only for non-action, so they diminish it day by day. Those who diminish it are still unable to avoid having an intention to act. One must even diminish the act of diminishing itself, and only then reach non-action. Non-action is what is called being still and not moving. Non-doing-nothing is what is called being moved and then penetrating all the reasons of the world. Engaging in the Way until one reaches this state is called "exceeding learning without worry," which is called "spirit without boundaries," and "change without body." If it is not the most spiritual thing in the world, who can participate in this? Looking at it from this perspective, taking the world is always done through non-action. It is clear that once one acts, it is insufficient to take the world.

<column-break/>

<margin>Commentary by Huang Maocai</margin> Only after knowing everything can one speak of learning, so learning desires to increase day by day. Once one is transformed, one can speak of the Way, so the Way desires to diminish day by day. However, that which increases can be sought through advancement, while that which diminishes may be difficult to force. Only those who are extremely clear can suddenly let go and drop everything, reaching the stage of non-action. Thus, they are able to do nothing while leaving nothing undone, and their applications are inexhaustible, acting upon the world with ease.

<margin>Commentary by Xizhai</margin> Engaging in learning is for the sake of seeking knowledge, hence the daily increase. Engaging in the Way is for the sake of removing falsehood, hence the daily decrease. If knowledge does not reach the limit, the decrease is not complete; therefore, the daily increase is the foundation for the daily decrease. If one diminishes and diminishes further until falsehood is gone and truth is complete, then one arrives at non-action. When one reaches non-action, every action one takes is never without it. This is no longer something that can be discussed in terms of increase or decrease. When one reaches the ultimate of non-action, even if the world is vast, it is unified by a single thread. If one creates affairs through having intent, even a single object before one’s eyes will be tangled and discordant, let alone the vastness of the world.

The Sage has no fixed heart; he takes the hearts of the common people as his own heart. For those who are good, I treat them with goodness; for those who are not good, I also treat them with goodness. Virtue is good. For those who are sincere, I treat them with sincerity; for those who are not sincere, I also treat them with sincerity. Virtue is sincere. <summary>This page presents scholarly commentaries on the concepts of "daily increase" (learning) and "daily decrease" (returning to the Way) in the context of Taoist non-action, followed by the beginning of chapter 49 of the Tao Te Ching.</summary>
